items.naslov: Cibona je prvak Hrvatske. Dvadeset i prvi put, i ovaj put s pričom koju pamtimo
items.seo_naslov: Cibona prvak Hrvatske 2026 — 21. naslov, majstorica protiv Zadra
items.meta_opis: Cibona je pobijedila Zadar 82:75 u petoj utakmici finala i osvojila 21. naslov prvaka Hrvatske. Navijačka kolumna Nermina Sefića o povijesnom uspjehu.
items.tekst:
Dvadeset i prvi put u povijesti kluba, Cibona je prvak Hrvatske. Ne na papiru,
ne lako — u petoj, odlučujućoj utakmici finalne serije, na gostovanju u
zadarskom Višnjiku, pred punim tribinama koje su navijale za domaćina.
Vukovi su pobijedili 82:75 i prekinuli Zadrov niz od tri uzastopna naslova.

Utakmica je bila upravo onakva kakvu navijač poželi da pamti. Zadar je vodio
dugo, Cibona je čekala svoj trenutak i preuzela kontrolu u završnici — u
posljednjim sekundama, kad je razlika pala na samo četiri poena, momčad nije
popustila. To je razlika između momčadi koja je htjela pobijediti i momčadi
koja je znala kako.

Justin Roberson, Žan Mark Šiško, Luka Skorić i Jan Palokaj nosili su teret
cijele serije, a u presudnim trenucima petog susreta baš su oni odlučivali
napade. Krešimir Radovčić je nakon utakmice rekao rečenicu koja govori više
od bilo koje statistike — da je momčad krenula s njih šestero na prvom
treningu krajem kolovoza, i da cijelu godinu nije bilo ni jednog incidenta,
ni jedne svađe. Kad netko izgradi takvu atmosferu, naslov dolazi kao
posljedica, ne kao slučajnost.

Posebno vrijedi spomenuti da je pobjeda došla u sezoni u kojoj je klub
prolazio kroz veliku transformaciju izvan terena — preoblikovanje u dioničko
društvo pod vodstvom Victora Dodiga. Sportski uspjeh usred organizacijske
promjene nije čest, i to dodatno govori o karakteru ove generacije igrača i
stožera.

Ovo je bila utakmica koja se pamti, i sezona koja se pamti. Vukovi su
pokazali da znaju i da mogu — dvadeset i prvi put, i ovaj put s pričom
vrijednom prepričavanja.
items.naslov_en: Cibona Is Croatian Champion. Twenty-First Time, and This One We'll Remember
items.seo_naslov_en: Cibona Croatian Champions 2026 — 21st Title, Thriller Against Zadar
items.meta_opis_en: Cibona beat Zadar 82:75 in game five of the finals to win their 21st Croatian championship. A fan column by Nermin Sefić on a historic win.
items.tekst_en:
For the twenty-first time in the club's history, Cibona is champion of Croatia. Not on paper, not easily — in a decisive fifth game of the finals series, on the road at Zadar's Visnjik arena, in front of a full house cheering for the home team. The Wolves won 82:75, ending Zadar's run of three straight titles.

This was exactly the kind of game a fan wants to remember. Zadar led for long stretches, and Cibona waited for its moment, taking control in the closing minutes — with the gap down to just four points in the final seconds, the team didn't fold. That's the difference between a team that wanted to win and a team that knew how.

Justin Roberson, Zan Mark Sisko, Luka Skoric and Jan Palokaj carried the weight of the whole series, and it was exactly them deciding possessions in the decisive moments of game five. Krešimir Radovčić said something after the game that speaks louder than any statistic — that the team started with just the six of them at the first training session in late August, and that across the entire year there wasn't a single incident, not one argument. When someone builds an atmosphere like that, the title arrives as a consequence, not a coincidence.

It's especially worth noting that this win came in a season when the club was going through a major transformation off the court — the restructuring into a joint-stock company under Victor Dodig's leadership. Sporting success in the middle of organizational change isn't common, and that says even more about the character of this generation of players and staff.

This was a game to remember, and a season to remember. The Wolves showed they know how, and that they can — twenty-one times now, and this time with a story worth retelling.

items.naslov: Cibona kutak: Victor Dodig i novo doba kluba
items.seo_naslov: Cibona kutak: Victor Dodig i novo doba kluba
items.meta_opis: Navijačka kolumna Nermina Sefića (GNK ASG) o Ciboni — pobjede, igrači tjedna i preoblikovanje kluba pod Victorom Dodigom.
items.tekst:
Cibona je ove sezone tamo gdje njezini navijači vole da bude — u igri za
najviše, s momčadi koja zna zagristi kad je najteže. Polufinale kupa i treće
mjesto na ljestvici Premijer lige nisu slučajnost; to je rezime tjedana u
kojima su pojedinci nosili momčad kad je trebalo.

Žan Marko Sisko je ove sezone potvrdio ono što navijači na tribinama već
znaju — bez lopte u njegovim rukama, ritam momčadi je drugačiji. Petnaest
asistencija protiv Alkara govori samo za sebe.

Krešimir Radovčić je pokazao da starenje u košarci ne mora značiti
usporavanje: dvadeset i šest poena protiv Splita, u trenutku kad je momčadi
trebala mirna ruka. Marijan Čakarun je te iste večeri dokazao da se borba
pod obručima ne mjeri centimetrima nego srcem — dvanaest skokova na
gostovanju kod Kvarnera. A Jan Palokaj svojim je rukama, ne riječima,
pokazao koliko vrijedi obrana koja krade lopte kad je najpotrebnije.

Bit će i tjedana kad rezultat ne ide po volji — takva je sezona, takav je
sport. Ali ovaj kutak postoji za jedno: da se ne zaboravi zašto se navija.

O Victoru Dodigu i preoblikovanju kluba — osobna procjena. Ono što se ovih
mjeseci događa s Cibonom nije samo još jedna transakcija u hrvatskom sportu
— to je trenutak koji pamtiš. Imao sam čast osobno se upoznati i družiti s
Victorom Dodigom, i ono što mogu reći nakon tog susreta jest da Cibona u
njemu ne dobiva investitora koji traži brzi povrat, nego čovjeka koji ovu
priču doživljava emotivno, kao poziv, ne kao ulaganje.

Slobodna procjena, ali procjena koja se teško može osporiti: preoblikovanje
Cibone iz udruge u dioničko društvo veliki je korak naprijed — ne samo za
klub, nego za cijelu hrvatsku košarku. Model koji je desetljećima donosio
neizvjesnost i gomilanje dugova napokon ustupa mjesto transparentnom,
kapitaliziranom vlasništvu.

Dodig za to ima i osobnu i profesionalnu težinu — čovjek koji godinama vodi
jednu od najvećih sjevernoameričkih banaka ne ulazi u ovakav pothvat
nasumično. Zasluge dijeli i Abraham Mišetić, čovjek koji je Dodiga i doveo
u priču, kao i Tomislav Šerić, koji klub vodi kroz ovu tranziciju.

Ovome tepihu dobrodošlice pridružujem se i osobno, s uvjerenjem da klub s
takvim vlasnikom iza sebe ima priliku vratiti se tamo gdje mu je mjesto.
items.naslov_en: Cibona Corner: Victor Dodig and a New Era for the Club
items.seo_naslov_en: Cibona Corner: Victor Dodig and the Club's New Era
items.meta_opis_en: A fan column by Nermin Sefić (GNK ASG) on Cibona — wins, the player of the week, and the club's restructuring under Victor Dodig.
items.tekst_en:
This season, Cibona is exactly where its fans want it to be — in the fight for the top, with a team that knows how to bite down when things get hardest. A cup semifinal and third place in the Premier League standings are no accident; they're the sum of weeks in which individuals carried the team when it mattered.

Zan Mark Sisko confirmed this season what fans in the stands already know — without the ball in his hands, the team's rhythm is simply different. Fifteen assists against Alkar speaks for itself.

Krešimir Radovčić showed that aging in basketball doesn't have to mean slowing down: twenty-six points against Split, at a moment the team needed a steady hand. Marijan Cakarun proved that same night that the fight under the rim isn't measured in centimeters but in heart — twelve rebounds on the road against Kvarner. And Jan Palokaj showed with his hands, not words, how much a defense that steals the ball is worth when it's needed most.

There will be weeks when the result doesn't go our way — that's the nature of a season, that's the nature of sport. But this corner exists for one reason: so we don't forget why we cheer.

On Victor Dodig and the club's restructuring — a personal take. What's happening with Cibona these months isn't just another transaction in Croatian sport — it's a moment you remember. I had the honor of personally meeting and spending time with Victor Dodig, and what I can say after that meeting is that Cibona isn't gaining an investor looking for a quick return, but a man who experiences this story emotionally, as a calling, not an investment.

A personal assessment, but one that's hard to dispute: restructuring Cibona from an association into a joint-stock company is a major step forward — not just for the club, but for Croatian basketball as a whole. A model that for decades brought uncertainty and mounting debt is finally giving way to transparent, capitalized ownership.

Dodig brings both personal and professional weight to this — a man who has spent years running one of the largest North American banks doesn't enter a venture like this randomly. Credit is also due to Abraham Misetic, the man who brought Dodig into the story, as well as Tomislav Seric, who is guiding the club through this transition.

I join this welcome myself, personally, with the conviction that a club with an owner like this behind it has the chance to return to where it belongs.

items.naslov: Umjetna inteligencija nije alat za velike. Zato je opasna za male koji je ignoriraju.
items.seo_naslov: AI za male tvrtke — zašto je čekanje skuplje od pogreške
items.meta_opis: Zašto je umjetna inteligencija opasnija za male tvrtke koje je ignoriraju nego za one koje kasne s usvajanjem.
items.tekst:
Svaki tjedan netko me pita treba li njegova tvrtka umjetnu inteligenciju. Pitanje
je pogrešno postavljeno. Ne treba se pitati treba li je se koristiti, nego koliko
dugo si tvrtka može priuštiti da je ne koristi.

Najveća zabluda o AI-ju jest da je to alat za velike sustave s velikim
budžetima. U praksi je suprotno. Velika tvrtka može apsorbirati godinu dana
neefikasnosti i nitko to neće primijetiti u bilanci. Mala tvrtka nema taj
luksuz. Svaki sat uložen u ručno rješavanje problema koji se može automatizirati
jest sat koji njezin konkurent, negdje drugdje, već ne troši.

Vidio sam to izbliza. U grupi radimo s poduzećima iz šest različitih
djelatnosti — od energetike do zdravstva — i obrazac je posvuda isti. Tvrtke
koje su prve posegnule za automatizacijom nisu bile najbogatije. Bile su
najnestrpljivije. Vlasnik koji je odbijao platiti trećeg zaposlenika za posao
koji softver radi jednako dobro, danas ima maržu kakvu njegov konkurent iz
susjedstva ne razumije kako postići.

Ono što me brine nije brzina usvajanja — ona je, iznenađujuće, dobra. Brine me
kvaliteta razumijevanja. Vidim tvrtke koje kupuju alat, ne mijenjaju proces, i
onda se čude što rezultat izostaje. AI ne popravlja loš proces. On ga ubrzava,
uključujući i njegove greške. Tko automatizira kaos, dobije brži kaos.

Postoji i drugi ekstrem, jednako čest: paraliza pred izborom. Deset alata, sto
webinara, nijedna odluka. Ovdje vrijedi staro pravilo poduzetništva —
manje važno je koji alat izabereš, važnije je da izabereš i počneš mjeriti.
Prvi mjesec neće biti savršen. Ali prvi mjesec s podacima vrijedi više od
šest mjeseci razmišljanja bez njih.

Za male i srednje tvrtke poruka je jednostavna, iako neugodna: ovo nije
tehnološki hir koji će proći. Ovo je promjena razine na kojoj se konkurencija
odvija. Tko čeka da bude jeftinije, sigurnije ili jasnije, čekat će dok
razlika između njega i konkurencije ne postane prevelika da je nadoknadi.

Nisam optimist zato što vjerujem u tehnologiju samu po sebi. Optimist sam
zato što znam koliko je poduzetnika u ovoj zemlji spremno raditi razliku
između preživljavanja i rasta — čim im netko pokaže da razlika postoji.
items.naslov_en: Artificial Intelligence Isn't a Tool for the Big Players. That's Exactly Why It's Dangerous for Small Ones Who Ignore It
items.seo_naslov_en: AI for Small Businesses — Why Waiting Costs More Than a Mistake
items.meta_opis_en: Why artificial intelligence is more dangerous for small businesses that ignore it than for those still catching up on adoption.
items.tekst_en:
Every week someone asks me whether their company needs artificial intelligence. It's the wrong question. The question isn't whether to use it, but how long your company can afford not to.

The biggest misconception about AI is that it's a tool for large systems with large budgets. In practice it's the opposite. A big company can absorb a year of inefficiency and no one will notice it on the balance sheet. A small company doesn't have that luxury. Every hour spent manually solving a problem that could be automated is an hour its competitor, somewhere else, is no longer spending.

I've seen this up close. Across our group we work with businesses in six different industries — from energy to healthcare — and the pattern is the same everywhere. The companies that reached for automation first weren't the wealthiest. They were the most impatient. An owner who refused to pay for a third employee to do work software does just as well now has a margin his neighborhood competitor can't figure out how to match.

What worries me isn't the speed of adoption — that's, surprisingly, good. What worries me is the quality of understanding. I see companies buy a tool, don't change the process, and then wonder why the results don't show up. AI doesn't fix a bad process. It accelerates it, mistakes included. Automate chaos, and you get faster chaos.

There's an equally common opposite extreme: paralysis in the face of choice. Ten tools, a hundred webinars, not a single decision. Here an old rule of entrepreneurship applies — which tool you pick matters less than picking one and starting to measure. The first month won't be perfect. But a first month with data is worth more than six months of thinking without it.

For small and mid-sized businesses the message is simple, if uncomfortable: this isn't a passing technological fad. It's a shift in the level at which competition happens. Whoever waits for it to become cheaper, safer, or clearer will wait until the gap between them and the competition becomes too large to close.

I'm not an optimist because I believe in technology for its own sake. I'm an optimist because I know how many entrepreneurs in this country are ready to make the difference between surviving and growing — the moment someone shows them that the difference exists.
